cards.explanation: The answer is False. Nadab and Abihu, two of Aaron's four sons, died before their father did, and the text says plainly that they had no sons. This is a heavy line. That's why the work falls to Eleazar and Ithamar, who “…served as priests.”

The answer is the roles they served in. David, with help from Zadok and Ahimelech, “…divided them according to the offices of their service.” So it's all about the jobs, friends. Like sorting a pile of cookie cutters by what they do, not by what shelf they came from.

The answer is eight. The text says there were “…sixteen heads of families from the descendants of Eleazar and eight from the descendants of Ithamar.” Do the math with me, bakers. Sixteen is exactly double eight. I bet somebody in that room double-checked the count.
The answer is by casting lots. The text says, “Thus they were divided by lot…” So the drawing set the order, friends. I think that's about as fair as a drawing gets.

The answer is that both sides had officers of the sanctuary. That's the reason the text gives. It says “…there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both Eleazar’s and Ithamar’s descendants.” So both sides had officers, and both went into the same drawing. Eleazar's side had sixteen heads of families to Ithamar's eight, yet the lots still covered them both.

The answer is king. The text says Shemaiah the scribe recorded the names “…in the presence of the king and of the officers…” The king there is David. So the names went down on the page with the king right there watching, friends.

The answer is False. The text says the names were recorded “…one family being taken from Eleazar, and then one from Ithamar.” So the two sides took turns being picked, bakers. Ithamar's side didn't have to sit and wait for sixteen of Eleazar's to go by.

The answer is their forefather Aaron. The text says this was their order for service “…according to the regulations prescribed for them by their forefather Aaron, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.” So the rules trace back to Aaron, and the text says the LORD had commanded him. Twenty-four families, one set of regulations. Now THAT is a well-run bakery.

The answer is True. The text says the regulations came from Aaron, “…as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.” So they weren't just Aaron's own ideas, friends. They followed what the LORD had commanded him.

The answer is that they cast lots like the priests. The text says “As their brothers the descendants of Aaron did, they also cast lots in the presence of King David and of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites…” Same method for everybody, bakers. The king and those leaders were right there for it.

The answer is False. The verse says they cast lots “…the family heads and their younger brothers alike.” Alike means the heads and the younger brothers were treated the same, friends. The lot did the picking, and the lot didn't care who was in charge.
